title: Introduce reservoir-based session sampler and fidelity validator for mixed-concurrency workloads
author: Maya Thompson
release_notes: Add a reservoir-based session sampler and a fidelity validator harness that produces per-kernel latency histograms and parquet exports; non-breaking, opt-in via CLI flag
description:
Motivation: We need a lightweight sampling mechanism that can produce a reproducible, statistically representative subset of sessions for long-running mixed-concurrency experiments (multi-tenant and mixed seq/latency workloads). Existing deterministic walnut replayers and stratified samplers either require full session retention or bias toward heavy hitters. This PR introduces a reservoir-based session sampler combined with a fidelity validator that compares golden traces against sampled runs to detect regression at kernel and hotspot level.

What this PR does (single continuous description): Adds a reservoir sampler component (rust) that streams session metadata and maintains a bounded sample set with deterministic seeding for reproducible runs. The sampler supports weight-decay to prefer recent sessions when requested and exposes a JSONL export for selected session priming sequences. A new fidelity-validator (python) consumes exported sessions, replays them against target binaries (local runner or k8s canary), and emits per-kernel and per-sequence latency histograms (tdigest + p50/p90/p99) and a delta report against a golden baseline. Exports are written as partitioned parquet files and a compact summary JSON that the existing reporting pipeline can ingest. The validator includes an optional eBPF probe integration to capture kernel-level tail events when running in privileged CI nodes. Also added a dashboard-skeleton (Grafana provisioned) and a minimal Jupyter notebook example for analysis.

Checklist:
- [x] Reservoir sampler implementation (rust) with deterministic seed option
- [x] JSONL export schema and validation tests
- [x] Fidelity validator harness (python) with tdigest histograms and parquet output
- [x] eBPF capture integration guard-flag (opt-in)
- [x] CI unit + integration tests (simulated replay)
- [x] Documentation: README, quickstart, dashboard notes
- [x] End-to-end smoke test in perf-canary

High level commits included: see commits list.

Files/areas changed (high level):
- src/sampler/reservoir.rs (new): core reservoir algorithm + deterministic seeding + weight decay
- tools/sampler-cli (new): small Rust binary for streaming selection and exporting JSONL samples
- validators/fidelity/validator.py (new): replay harness, tdigest aggregation, parquet exporter
- validators/fidelity/ebpf_probe.py (new, optional import guarded): eBPF sampler utilities for privileged nodes
- reporting/parquet_writer.py (modified): add partitioning helper and schema registration for sampler exports
- docs/benchmarking/reservoir-sampler.md (new) and docs/benchmarking/fidelity-validator.md (new)
- perf-canary/configs/reservoir-smoke.yml (new): smoke canary job definition
- tests/unit/test_reservoir.py (new) and tests/integration/test_validator_smoke.py (new)
- dashboards/provisioning/reservoir-fidelity.json (new): Grafana skeleton dashboard

Notes on design decisions: The sampler is stream-first and never requires materializing the full session log; deterministic reproducibility is achieved by combining a run-seed with a stable hash of session metadata. Weight decay is implemented by adjusting selection probability by e^(−age/half_life) so you can trade recency for representativeness. The fidelity validator uses tdigest to keep memory bounded and parquet to make downstream analytics cheap. eBPF capture is optional and gated behind --enable-ebpf; we do not attempt to alter runner behavior when eBPF is disabled.

Testing and CI: Unit tests for reservoir properties (unbiased in limit, reproducibility) and validator aggregation correctness were added. Integration smoke test runs a short in-process replay with an instrumented toy model (perf fixture) and validates the parquet schema can be read by the reporting pipeline. CI matrix: linux-rust, linux-python, macos-smoke. CI initially flaked on eBPF tests (privilege) so those are skipped on non-privileged runners; CI green after skip.

Backward compatibility: The sampler and validator are opt-in. Existing ingestion and replay flows are unchanged; an adapter was added to the reporting pipeline to accept partitioned parquet exports. No breaking changes to API or existing workload runners.

Migration/Usage notes: To try locally: 1) build sampler-cli, 2) stream sessions from an existing event log with --seed to make sample deterministic, 3) run validator.py --input-samples out.jsonl --target-binary ./local-runner --output /tmp/fidelity.parquet. See docs for full examples.

Related work and followups: This PR lays groundwork for a scheduled sampler job for long-term drift detection (ENG-7489). Followups include: automatic cohort selection by traffic shape, richer regression alerting in console, and tighter integration with canary control plane.

Review summary and rationale for merge: Reviewed for algorithmic correctness, memory/cpu bounds, and opt-in safety; reviewers approved after two iterations addressing doc clarity, adding a defensive timeout for replay loops, and skipping eBPF on unprivileged CI. Merged via squash.

notes_for_maintainers: Sampler state is intentionally minimal; if you need stateful drift tracking across runs, persist the JSONL exports to long-term storage. When enabling eBPF in CI, ensure the runner has CAP_SYS_ADMIN and that tests run in isolated VMs.
